prerequisites: General processor structure, principle, function of particular blocks
Data and code memories, static and dynamic RAM, ROM, PROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash EEPROM, FRAM memories
Data, address and control bus, multiplexed bus, three state and open collector bus drivers
Asynchronous events servicing, polling/interrupt. Interrupt system, priority, interrupt vector, interrupt service routine, application
Digital output, interfacing, accommodation, optical separation, Switching ON and OFF of induction and resistive load
Digital input, interfacing, accommodation, optical separation
D/A converters. Principle of PWM modulation, converter uses operation amplifier
A/D converter uses integrator principle. Single and double integration converters
Feedback A/D converters - incremental, tracking converter, converters with succeeded approximation
Unified voltage and current signal
Parallel data transfer, handshake principle, examples of communication (e.g. Centronics interface)
Serial data transfer, protocol TIA/EIA 232, data format, speed, signal levels
Industrial standards TIA/EIA 422, 423 and 485. Simplex, half duplex and full duplex communication.
Principle and using a MODEM for data transfer. Modulation, band width, modulation and transfer speed. Baud, bit/s
Mictroprocessor familu 8051/52, internal architecture. Data and code memory. SFR registers
External memory and periphery extension for 8051 processors. Data and code memory, address decoder, data flow, transfer control
Interrupt system of 8051 family. Sources, levels and priorities of interrupts
Counters and timers, serial port 8051's processors
Assembler, source text format, directives for translation control
Proceeding program, tools for program development, SW simulators, HW emulators
Translation, linking, locations. Object, absolute, relative code. Data hex format Libraries
Numeric systems, binary, decimal, hexadecimal. BCD coding. Conversion between numeric systems. Negative numbers notation
Direct, indirect, relative and absolute addressing. Examples of using
Internal and external address areas of 8051 family
Arithmetic and logic instructions of 8051 family
Instructions for data transfer of 8051 family
Instructions for jumps and subroutine calls of 8051 family

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the history of computers and microcomputers.
Understand the block diagram of a computer.
Understand busses, processors, memories, input and output circuits.
Understand instruction sets, machine code, assembler, and ANSY-C language.
Understand software and hardware tools for application development, including simulator, emulator, and logical analyzer.
Understand computer interfaces, converters, digital input and output.
Understand analogous signal discretization, methods and errors of D/A and A/D conversion, and standard analogous signals.
Gain practical experience with the 8051/52 microcomputer family through laboratory work.

syllabus_topics: Introduction into microcomputer programming - basic concepts, registers, memories
Serial and parallel interfaces, buses for data transfer
Basic data, numerical systems, data presentation, binary operations as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division
Using Keil IDE for I51, 1st semester work setting
1st semester work solving and its verification
Development tool kit BAST166 and programming in ANSY-C
Development tool kit BAST166 and programming in ANSY-C, examples
Intelligent servo drive AtlasCopco, basic features and programming, 2nd semester work setting
